[tool_result: 301	- **NOTE ADDED WHILE IN PRESS (in the 1939 pamphlet, discovered while proofs were being set):** While the pamphlet was being set up in type, Rundle was allowed to look at the Association's old ledgers in the office on another errand. The station account carries every year an entry in the bookkeeper's hand: "Ostrey Hollow: butter fat credited to patrons on station test, 57,760 lb. Butter fat received at Larrow Green in station cream, 60,800 lb. Station gain, 3,040 lb, five and a quarter per cent, as usual. Carried to the general account." Rundle noted: "I must go back on Chapter IV. Cream stolen at the Hollow would have reached the Green light. It reached the Green heavy, every year, and I cannot make my paragraph stand. I leave it as written and correct it here." This represents Rundle's revision in the press, acknowledging that the heavy receipt of cream at Larrow Green contradicted the theft theory, and he corrected the record while the book was being published.

303	**Alonzo Frick** (Attorney, board chairman, Ordell County Bar Association)
304	- At seventy-four (in 1946), wrote article for Ordell County Bar Association yearbook
305	- Tried titles and boundaries for forty years, and two homicides
306	- Ostrey Hollow matter stayed with him more than anything he argued in courthouse
307	- Named chairman of board of arbitration (one of three), possibly because he kept no cow
308	- Sat three times: first session 17 March 1925 at Association's office at Ashlin; second and third sessions asked to have at Ostrey Hollow itself in station's own weigh room
309	- Board satisfied itself on all physical appliances; saw scales tried, sampling and test done, never saw anything hidden
310	- Board heard three explanations: (1) water by Selby Vose; (2) tester taking cream and writing low tests by Wilbur Teague; (3) wet hay/bog meadow by 1908 committee report read into record
311	- Ansel Keddie made statement to board on 17 March 1925
312	- Ansel denied taking cream and said he tested as taught and as state man had seen him do it, thirty-one times a week for twenty-nine seasons; believed him then and believes him now; his denial accurate but did him no good because man who cannot account for a figure presumed by everybody to be figure's author
313	- **Private corridor conversation at Ashlin with Keddie:** Ansel told Frick he always thought patrons at fault and would not say so in room; lived among them thirty years and would not stand up and accuse neighbors; recorded because it has been said since that Keddie went to grave accusing nobody (true) and suspecting nobody (not true)
314	- **Dismissal while board sitting (April 30, 1925, four days before award):** Association dismissed Ansel without finding against him; board had not concluded and did not conclude he did anything whatever; simply let go while board still sitting; Frick never able to think well of Association for it
315	- **May 4, 1925 award:** Found no cause established and awarded Ostrey Hollow patrons $3,800 without admission to be charged to station account; patrons' own reckoning of loss was 67,000 pounds butterfat over years complained of; nothing brought forward to disturb that figure; board not able to say who owed it or why; said so
316	- Award without finding is unsatisfactory thing; every member of board knew it
317	- **Exhibits before board (four books and nothing else):**
318	  1. Test book of Ostrey Hollow station, 4 May 1896 to 31 December 1924, in hand of Ansel Keddie
319	  2. Receiving book of said station
320	  3. Private weigh book of Emmet Brant of Hessel Bottom, begun 1 January 1897
321	  4. Circuit notebook of state dairy inspector for year 1923
322	- Short list for matter of that size; looked at it many times since
323	- **Reflection:** Board can only decide between accounts put to it; three were put to board; each urged by man of standing; each would have been believed by half valley; not one proved
324	- Wondered since whether answer was in that room]
